newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore telecoms beauty contest wide open.
newsitem.headline: Singapore telecoms beauty contest wide open.

text.p: Several of the world's biggest telecommunications firms are battling for a licence to offer new fixed-wire telephone services in Singapore from April 2000.
But the right to compete with the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, may not go to the strongest bidder and analysts said on Wednesday the competition was still wide open.
"Bidding is basically a beauty contest," said Gautam Kapoor, regional telecoms analyst at ING Baring. "It is not driven by financial considerations but by who can offer the best service."
Singapore, with a population of just three million, is a tiny market by world standards. But it offers potentially lucrative rewards to any international telecoms operator.

As one of Asia's biggest financial markets, the island is the regional base for thousands of multi-national corporations generating huge business demand. It is also the hub for telecoms cable networks across Southeast Asia.
Three consortiums have do far thrown their hat into the ring ahead of the May 31 deadline for initial proposals for pre-qualification in the licence tender.

Britain's second biggest telecoms company, Cable and Wireless Plc (C&W), confirmed on Tuesday it would bid for a licence with its unit Hong Kong Telecommunications, Singapore conglomerate Keppel Corp and newspaper publisher Singapore Press Holdings Ltd.
This consortium already runs Singapore's second mobile phone service, MobileOne (M1).

C&W's arch-rival, British Telecommunications Plc (BT), has already signed up to bid with Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), and state-owned firms Singapore Power (SP) and Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT).

Local industrial conglomerate SembCorp and state-owned railway company Singapore MRT Ltd (SMRT) have also said they may bid and are looking for foreign partners. Foreign investment in any licence bid will be limited to 49 percent.
On the face of it, the strongest bid for the one or two licences the Singapore government has said it will award next year is from the BT/NTT/SP/STT combination.

With its recently announced merger with the United States' second carrier MCI, BT has a global reach and the four companies together could offer competitive services and large financial reserves for the construction of local infrastructure.
But analysts say they have no idea how the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS) will select the winner.

"TAS will have to decide which combination can bring most to telephone customers and the relative power of the companies will be less important than their plans, particularly for niche markets," said David Riedel, analyst at Solomon in Bangkok.
And with two weeks left before initial bids have to be submitted, there are rumours new players may enter the race.
One or all of the members of the Global One alliance of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom are reported to be talking to SembCorp/SMRT.
There are also rumours that an unnamed fourth consortium of U.S. and European partners may come in at the last moment.
"We still don't even know whether there will be one or two new licences," said Riedel. "And it is impossible to say how TAS will make its decision."
TAS has said any new licencee must offer a full telecoms service, which analysts say will cost Singapore $500 million (US$347 million) to S$1 billion in initial investment. ($1 = S$1.44)
